name: Seonodo Lite
author: Adriano Di Stasi

sections.description:
Seonodo Lite does the part of SEO that is mechanical and has a right answer: the tags in the head, the structured data, the sitemap, the robots file, the canonical addresses, the redirects. It then adds the one file written for language models rather than crawlers — llms.txt.

It talks to no server of ours. There is no account, no licence check and no update channel of its own: every request the plugin makes goes to the site it is installed on.

What it does

Meta tags. An SEO title and description per page, with a live search-result preview in the editor and a character count against what search engines actually show. Open Graph and X/Twitter tags for sharing, a default share image, and per-page robots control. Verification tags for Google Search Console, Bing and Yandex.

Structured data. One JSON-LD graph per page rather than a pile of separate blocks: Organization or LocalBusiness, WebSite with its internal search, Article, BreadcrumbList, VideoObject for embedded YouTube and Vimeo, and Service for businesses that sell services. A page where you have written your own schema keeps it — the automatic main entity steps aside instead of declaring the same thing twice. Opening hours are parsed properly, including Mo,We,Fr 09:00-13:00, which most parsers split on the comma and lose two days to.

XML sitemaps. An index plus paginated sitemaps for posts, pages, custom post types and taxonomies, with images, optional language alternatives, and news and video sitemaps when you need them. Built on request and cached, so a new page appears without anyone regenerating anything, and rebuilt twice a day in the background so a crawler finds it ready. Pages marked as excluded stay out, and the settings page tells you how many items each type contributes and why anything was left out — including when another plugin is filtering the query behind your back.

robots.txt. An editor with templates, served through WordPress rather than written to disk, so there is no stale file left behind and no write access needed. The sitemap line is kept correct automatically: WordPress adds its own line pointing at the core sitemap, and that one sends crawlers to the wrong file.

AI crawlers. The crawlers run by AI companies do three different jobs, and the plugin keeps them apart, because the difference decides what happens to you. One collects training data. One indexes you so you can appear in an AI answer. One fetches a single page while answering one person’s question. Blocking the second or third does not protect you from training — it removes you from the answers. The presets say so in those words.

llms.txt. A plain-text map of your site written for language models: what the site is, who it is for, and the pages worth reading, as links. Served at /llms.txt from a rewrite rule, so it is always current. A page you kept out of the sitemap stays out of this too — marking something as not worth indexing did not mean “hide it from Google but hand it to the models”.

Redirects and not-found addresses. A log of what visitors ask for and do not find, with a hit counter so the ones worth a redirect stand out from the noise, and addresses that already have a redirect hidden from the list. One button turns a logged address into a redirect. Rules support 301, 302, 307 and 410 Gone, can be paused without deleting them, and you can supply your own page for retired content.

A status screen, not a form. The first thing the plugin shows is what it is doing on this site right now: how many addresses are in the sitemap, how many pages are in llms.txt, which structured data types are being published, whether robots.txt is being answered by WordPress or overridden by a real file. If the rewrite rules are not in place yet — the reason /sitemap.xml returns 404 after activating — it says so there, with the link to fix it.

Quick Edit. The SEO title, description, robots setting and sitemap exclusion are editable straight from the posts list, without opening the editor. A description is a small thing to change and a large thing to open a page builder for, which is why most descriptions never get written.

A traffic light that does not lie. Each page gets green, amber or red, with the reasons. The checks are facts about the page — is there a description, will the title be truncated, do the images have alternative text, does the page link anywhere — and there is no keyword density rule anywhere in it. Green means nothing mechanical is left to fix. It does not mean the page will rank, and the plugin does not pretend otherwise.

A readable sitemap. [seonodo_lite_html_sitemap] puts one on any page.

On privacy

The not-found log stores the visitor’s address as a salted hash, never in the clear, using your site’s own salt. It exists only to tell two visitors apart and cannot be turned back into an address — which a plain SHA-256 of an IPv4 address can be, since there are only four billion of them.

The paid version

Seonodo, the paid plugin, adds the things that need an outside service or a lot of machinery: AI content generation with your own API keys, a GEO Monitor that checks whether ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews cite your site for the queries you choose, keyword rank tracking, cannibalisation detection, Search Console integration, Core Web Vitals from real visits, and a multi-site cloud panel. It is sold at adsnetwork.it.

Nothing here is time-limited, and nothing is switched off waiting for a payment. The two plugins share the same code for everything above, and they share the per-page fields: a site that starts on Lite and moves to Seonodo keeps every title, description and canonical it has written.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate.
  2. Open Seonodo Lite in the admin menu.
  3. On the General tab, fill in the home title and description and your search console verification codes.
  4. On the Sitemap tab, pick the post types and taxonomies that belong in the sitemap.
  5. On the Robots & AI crawlers tab, decide what the AI crawlers may do.

Nothing has to be configured for the plugin to be useful: the sitemap, the structured data and llms.txt work from the defaults.

If /sitemap.xml or /llms.txt returns a 404 right after activating, go to Settings → Permalinks and save once. That rebuilds the rewrite rules.
sections.faq:
Does it send anything anywhere?

No. Every request it makes goes to your own site — reading your sitemap to check it, for instance. There is no account, no licence check, no telemetry and no update server of ours.

Can I run it alongside another SEO plugin?

You can, but you should not for long: two plugins writing meta tags produce two titles, two descriptions and two canonicals on the same page, and search engines have to guess. The plugin reads the noindex flags set by Yoast, Rank Math and SEOPress so the sitemap agrees with them while you move across.

Can I run it alongside the paid Seonodo?

No, and it stops itself. The paid plugin includes everything here, so running both would write every tag twice. Lite notices and switches itself off with a notice rather than letting the site produce duplicate output.

Does it replace the WordPress core sitemap?

It leaves wp-sitemap.xml working, as a safety net, and declares only its own in robots.txt, so crawlers follow one of them. To switch the core one off: add_filter( 'seonodo_lite_disable_core_sitemap', '__return_true' );

Nothing on the Robots tab has any effect

There is a real robots.txt file in your site root, so the web server is serving that and WordPress is never asked. The tab tells you when it finds one. Delete the file.

What is llms.txt?

A convention for a plain-text file that tells a language model what a site is and which pages matter, the way robots.txt tells a crawler what it may fetch. The specification is at llmstxt.org. No AI company is obliged to read it; it costs nothing to publish and it is how you state what you want done with your content.

Can I add FAQ structured data?

The FAQPage block is built from the seonodo_lite_faq_items filter, so a theme or another plugin can supply the questions. There is no FAQ editor in Lite.

What happens to my work if I uninstall?

The plugin’s own settings and the not-found log are deleted. The SEO fields you wrote on each page are kept, so moving to the paid plugin keeps all of them. There is a setting on the Redirects tab to delete those too.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • Activation no longer rebuilt the rewrite rules before the plugin had registered its own, which left /llms.txt and the sitemaps answering 404 until Permalinks were saved by hand. The rebuild now happens on the first request after activation, once the routes exist.
  • The admin JavaScript moved out of the pages and into enqueued files: wp_enqueue_script() for the code, wp_add_inline_script() for the data.
  • JSON-LD is encoded with escaped slashes, so a </script> sequence inside a title or a description can no longer close the block early.
  • Quick Edit reads its values from a data attribute instead of a hidden JSON block.
  • The “Seonodo is already active” notice now appears only on the Plugins screen, and is dismissible.
  • The warning about invalid JSON in the schema box survives the save and is shown on the editor screen, where it was being lost to the redirect.
  • Translations are no longer bundled: they come from translate.wordpress.org.

1.1.2

  • JSON-LD is now printed with wp_print_inline_script_tag() instead of a hand-built <script> tag.
  • date() replaced with gmdate() for sitemap timestamps, so the output does not follow the server timezone.
  • File deletions go through wp_delete_file(); parse_url() replaced with wp_parse_url().
  • Added the missing translators: comments on plural strings.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1.

1.1.1

  • The SEO column was drawn twice on every row of the Pages list. WordPress fires two different hooks for pages, and the plugin was listening to both.

1.1.0

  • A status screen as the first thing the plugin shows, with the real numbers for this site and a warning when the rewrite rules are not in place yet.
  • Quick Edit: SEO title, description, robots and sitemap exclusion from the posts list, plus an SEO column showing what is missing at a glance.
  • A per-page traffic light with the reasons, built only from facts about the page. No keyword density, no writing-style rules.
  • Redirect rules are now editable: the engine was there, nothing in the interface reached it. One button turns a logged not-found address into a redirect.
  • robots.txt no longer corrupts paths written in a non-Latin alphabet. The sanitiser worked on bytes and kept only the Latin-1 range, which breaks the UTF-8 sequences that contain a byte between 0x80 and 0x9F.
  • llms.txt labels can no longer contain a line break, which would split one line of the file in two.

1.0.0

  • First release.
